children: New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- The Punjab National Bank (PNB) is going to revise several important charges starting tomorrow, i.e., 1 November, 2026, on its Visa and RuPay credit cards. This makes it vital for eligible PNB credit cardholders to stay informed and plan their use accordingly.

The charges will cover cash withdrawals, late payments, failed payment instructions, reward point redemptions, utility bill payments, and other associated charges. Some of the services that were previously free will incur charges.
This write-up is dedicated towards discussing these changes in detail, so that eligible PNB credit card holders remain better informed and prepared to plan their finances accordingly.
Here are the key changes cardholders should know.
Note: The charges discussed in the table above are illustrative. For complete details, refer to the official website of the lending institution

It is vital to keep in mind that the revised late payment fee is going to be decided by the total outstanding amount. No charge is going to be applied for dues of Rs.500 or less. It is going to rise to Rs.500 for dues of Rs.501 to Rs.1000, Rs.750 for Rs.1,001 to Rs.10,000, Rs.1,000 for Rs.10,001 to Rs.50,000 and Rs.1,200 for amounts above Rs.50,000.

The banking institution will impose a charge of Rs.100 per instrument for cheque or auto-debit failures on fixed deposit-linked cards. For these cards, late payment charges are going to remain at 30% of the minimum amount due,subject to a minimum of Rs.200 and a maximum of Rs.500 per billing cycle.

Furthermore, E-statements are going to remain free, whereas duplicate statements that are older than three months will attract charges of Rs.50 per month. All eligible PNB cardholders should diligently check and review their spending and payment habits before the revised fee structure takes effect.

Disclaimer: Charges discussed above are illustrative and may vary by card variant. Cardholders should refer to PNB's official website for the latest applicable fees and terms.
